q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a hydraulic cylinder?
title: Hydraulic cylinder carbon footprint per unit
short: Weigh the steel barrel, piston rod, end caps and seals per cylinder and multiply by supplier figures. Add honing, machining, chrome plating and assembly energy, then divide the plant's energy by cylinders made.

ul: Honed steel tube for the barrel.

p: Report per cylinder by bore, stroke and weight. If rods are chrome plated in-house, count the plating line's energy as well.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 45,580 / 3,000 = 15.2 kg CO2 per unit
Add steel tube, rod and seals for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
